scope: Independent source-only review of v2 VecDeque producer prototype
verdict: DO NOT ADOPT: typecheck and runtime behavior remain unverified, an existing required v14 control needs its separate fixture repair, and memory, scheduling and full producer ownership remain unqualified.
v1_finding: The v1 patch omitted the existing prepare_tests.rs while changing Worker.pending to VecDeque and adding receiving. Its untouched Worker initializer, Vec-only front/back calls and Vec remove return type made that test module incompatible by inspection. V2 adds corresponding mechanical adaptations; no Rust build was performed to establish v2 compiles.
independent_checks: Verified v14 source/catalog preimages, v2 postimages, original producer-test tail and prepare-test normalization, and exact patch forward/reverse with the supplied verifier.
Rustfmt 1.10.0-stable --check edition 2021 skip_children passed for all four v2 Rust files.
Inspected PendingView logical two-slice iteration, recv_many/absorb sequencing, split state and inverse restoration, Worker Drop order, and proposed test witnesses.

A Python model exercised 1012 small logical selection cases and 3123 partial-permutation rollback checkpoints; all restored original order. This does not execute Rust or exercise physical wraparound, allocator, callbacks or task cancellation.
source_observations: A successful recv_many is absorbed into the deque synchronously before account_pending_from awaits; Tokio 1.53.3 documents that a losing select branch receives no messages. V2 only has an unrun closed-worker test after successful receipt and accounting begins.

Suffix extraction uses synchronous VecDeque drain in forward logical order, not the reversed-pop sketch. Split rollback restores selected items before inverse permutation; selected-all conversion and wrapped capacity need runtime checks.

Old test assertions and identities were not deliberately removed; v2 still preserves the known v14 ordered-deadline fixture, which normally reaches Ready while that test expects Pending. Hosted panic details were unavailable, so this is a source-level explanation, not an observed panic diagnosis.
blocking_limits: The original v14 deadline-scan fixture repair is separate and must be reconciled against the eventual deque source; the original assertions and thresholds must remain.

Scratch Vec plus deque and spare batch retain peak capacity; there is no producer-wide count/byte bound, and synchronous absorb, batch drain, rollback, and Drop can be linear in configurable chunk/queue size.

Potential unwind window: absorb_received constructs a receiving.drain iterator before deque extension can reserve; a reserve panic can drop remaining accepted scratch items without Worker retirement accounting. Reserving before drain alone does not fix a potentially allocating Drop cleanup. Ordinary allocator OOM often aborts; no such unwind was observed.
Split::first removes a record before selected.push can allocate; this possible unwind issue also exists in the v14 Vec implementation and is not identified as a new regression.

Closed/open producer cleanup, callback/byte/sticky/retry sequence accounting, real select cancellation, wrapped all/suffix split cases, partial network writes, live Kafka and TLS/SASL remain untested.
No optimized queue or end-to-end benchmark was run; complexity analysis does not establish a speedup or the cause of the retained-backing failure.
limits: No Cargo, Rust compiler, Rust tests, Clippy, native Kafka, benchmark, publication or production qualification was performed.
The Python model is an independently written logical approximation of mixed split permutations, not a substitute for testing the actual code.
Source is pinned to v14, before the separate v16 deadline fixture work and release-checker changes.
